newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong's Tung meets China's foreign minister.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Tung meets China's foreign minister.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa arrived in Beijing on Wednesday to seek Chinese approval for his choices of top officials who will serve after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule in July.
Tung met China's Foreign Minister Qian Qichen at the Diaoyutai State Guest House in Beijing after his arrival from Hong Kong.
He was expected to meet Premier Li Peng later in the day.
On Tuesday, Tung said in Hong Kong he was confident China would approve his choice of top officials for his post-handover administration.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, will revert to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.

The outgoing British colonial administration has urged Tung to make as few changes as possible in the ranks of top civil servants, who hold positions akin to cabinet ministers in Britain and wield considerable power.

Tung won public acclaim when he invited Hong Kong's popular Chief Secretary, Anson Chan, head of the civil service and deputy to British Governor Chris Patten, to stay on, guaranteeing a measure of continuity in uncertain times.
Chan accepted, but the fate of her senior policy secretaries remains to be decided.
